Prospective Parents
Do you have a child starting school in September? Or perhaps your child is in an older year group and you’re looking for a new school community? We would love to welcome you!
Our school is more than just a place to learn – it’s a family where every child is valued, supported, and encouraged to thrive. If you’d like to see what makes our school so special, we warmly invite you to come for a tour. This is a wonderful opportunity to meet our staff, explore our classrooms, and discover the caring environment we offer.
To arrange your visit, please contact the school office on 01323 502525 or email office@heronppa.org.uk and we'll arrange a time for you to visit us. We can’t wait to meet you and share all the exciting things happening at our school!
If you would like your child to attend our school, please see full details of our admission arrangements below.
The local County Council makes arrangements for the admission of children to our school in the Reception year (4+ year olds).
You will need to apply for a place at the school you would like your child to attend – it doesn’t happen automatically. Even if your child already attends the nursery class of the school, or your older children go there, you will need to apply. You may not get a place at the same school if other children have priority.

SEND
SEND
Children learn in different ways and at different levels. Sometimes our children may need additional help, either to overcome a learning difficulty or to make sure that the curriculum fully extends.
Mrs Owen is our Assistant Headteacher for Inclusion (school SENCO) and works closely with parents and staff to provide support for our children with special educational needs or disabilities (SEND).
What is SEN?
To reach their full potential, some children need extra support, especially those who find learning challenging. These children may struggle with:
All of these can be a barrier to learning.
Depending on the level of need, a child may receive the following support:
Following lessons
Controlling their emotions
Their sensory or physical needs
Reading, writing and maths
Interacting with both adults and their peers
Expressing themselves
SEN Support
This describes the extra help given to a child to enable them to access the curriculum. It may include:
● Extra support within the classroom
● Small group or one-to-one learning
● Support from outside professionals, like Speech and Language therapists
EHC Plans
These are for children with more complex needs. It involves a formal request for assessment, from either the school or from parents, to the Local Authority.

pageCache.text:
Sports Premium
Sports Premium report
Curriculum Time PE
At Heron Park, we take great pride in our PE curriculum and after-school sports programme. The high quality of our sporting provision has been recognised in our last two Ofsted reports.
Alongside delivering rich, engaging PE lessons taught by our own teachers, we also offer a wide-ranging after-school sports programme. This commitment has helped the Academy develop a conveyor belt of successful teams, with our trophy cabinet serving as testament to their achievements.
The Academy achieves this by investing its PE and Sport Premium funding in our outdoor play provision, a high-quality PE scheme of work, and opportunities for children to participate in local competitions, including funding for transport and team kit.
All children receive one high-quality PE lesson each week:
Term 1 - 3 weeks Team Building Skills / OAA, 4 weeks Ball Skills / Invasion Games
Term 2 - 6 weeks Ball Skills / Invasion Games
Term 3 - 6 weeks Dance
Term 4 - 6 weeks Gymnastics
Term 5 - 6 weeks Athletics
Term 6 - 7 weeks Striking and Fielding Games / Over the Net Games
We also provide a variety of sports and dance after-school clubs through our sports provider, Infinite Sport, which are available to all pupils in Years 1 to 6. Activities range from dance and volleyball to football and gymnastics. The breadth of opportunities on offer ensures that there is something for everyone throughout the year.
In the 2025-2026 academic year, we were delighted to achieve the Silver School Games Mark, recognising our commitment to providing high-quality sporting opportunities for all pupils.

Curriculum
IMG_0064.JPG
Our Curriculum
Our broad and balanced curriculum is underpinned by our vision that all pupils reach their full potential, guided by our school motto: We care, we play, we grow, we always try our best. This ethos is reflected in everything we do, inspiring children to thrive both academically and personally.
As a school, we are committed to ensuring our pupils are confident in reading, writing and mathematics. We dedicate time each morning to these lessons to build our children's skills and knowledge in these areas. However, our rich and motivating curriculum extends beyond these core subjects with opportunities for all our pupils to develop their love of science, drama, music, art and geography, for example.
We follow the Aurora Academies Trust (AAT) curriculum for the foundation subjects within our school. Based on the statutory requirements for the National Curriculum, the AAT curriculum encourages enquiry at every stage. Skills and knowledge are mapped out across each subject progressively, enabling pupils to become confident mathematicians, writers, readers, scientists, historians, artists, geographers, programmers, designers, sports people, musicians by the time they leave our setting. Our ambitious curriculum builds on what our pupils already know and enables our children to gain the knowledge and skills they need in the next phase of their educational career and beyond. Parent have the right to remove thrive child from RE lessons.
Our pupils study topics across the school. Each topic is based on a key Concept Question which our children answer at the end of their unit of work. The questions the children explore are included in each of the progression documents which you can find in the link below.
At Heron Park, our values are at the heart of everything we do. Our engaging curriculum enables our children to be respectful, curious, independent, resilient, and aspirational during every moment of our school day.
Please use the links below to read our curriculum rationale and to view more details about the learning within each subject.
AAT Curriculum Rationale and Overview

pageCache.pageTitle: Heron Park Primary Academy - Pupil Premium
pageCache.text:
Pupil Premium
WHAT IS PUPIL PREMIUM?
The Pupil Premium is extra money paid to the school to help us give additional support to some children who may need it. The support can vary from teaching help to supporting a school trip.
The money is based on the number of children who are registered for Free School Meals, or have been registered at any time in the last 6 years.
HOW DO WE USE THE MONEY?
We do not use the money just to benefit children receiving Free School Meals, we try to help all children who we feel are vulnerable to under achievement. We do try to ensure that those children entitled to Free School Meals (FSM) who are vulnerable do receive the benefit of additional support.
The money is spent in many ways: we provide one to one tuition for some children, Maths and Literacy support and intervention through internal and / or external support, targeted work with specialist staff, extra Teaching Assistant time , booster groups either on a short term or long term basis as well as supporting trips and visitors to school to lead activities for the children.
The money is spent carefully and not used in the general budget. We make sure it is spent on supporting children who are vulnerable to under achievement.
Our Pupil Premium policy and actions are reviewed constantly throughout the year.
